conviction_note: This print is a debt event with earnings attached. The release comes the business day after the 1.75% converts (~$45.6m) mature on 2026-11-15, and the company says it moved the date specifically to report on its convertible debt discussions. abs_move is therefore set well above the 17.2% median reaction, at 30. p_up is 52 because the evidence is balanced. Scheduling a call (and a Box product release the next day) points away from a Chapter 11 the price may partly discount, and a crowded short supports that. Against that, cash of roughly $15-20m against $45.6m due means any resolution is likely dilutive or secured, and the FY guide needs an H2 ramp that Q2 does not support. The per-finding sum (-0.8) and the scaled number (+1.2) differ in sign only because the squeeze and survival-relief mechanisms enter p_up slightly above their filed sizes. Both are effectively zero on a 30-point move.
bar: Q3 2026 revenue consensus $25.6m (single source: Benzinga, https://www.benzinga.com/quote/VERI/earnings-forecasts; not confirmed by a second estimate source, so the reported-quarter bar is capped small). The company guide is FY2026 revenue of $100-115m and a non-GAAP net loss of $22-32m (Q2 release, 2026-08-13, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001615165/000162828026056736/veriearningsreleaseq22026e.htm). H1 revenue was $44.5m, so the guide implies H2 of $55.5-70.5m, or $27.8-35.3m a quarter against Q2's $24.3m. The real bar on this print is the outcome of the convertible maturity, which has no consensus.
positioning_check: FINRA short interest via Equibles (https://equibles.com/stocks/veri/shortinterest): 12.68m shares at the 2026-10-30 settlement, 7.78 days to cover, up from 12.15m on 10-15 and down from 18.17m on 09-15. Shares outstanding are about 122m (100.46m at 2026-08-11 + 1.3m ATM + 20m in the Oct registered direct), so short interest is about 10% of outstanding. Against StockTitan's 43.73m float figure (https://www.stocktitan.net/news/VERI/veritone-updates-date-of-third-quarter-2026-earnings-release-and-ji9vtie38wee.html) it would be about 29%; that float figure is possibly stale. Either way the short is crowded, with nearly 8 days to cover. Options: there is no usable chain (ATM spread 100% of mid, no skew); ATM IV is 306% and the put/call OI ratio 0.44 (call-heavy OI). Tape: the stock is at its all-time low, $0.46, -92.4% off the 52-week high, -14.8% over 20 days and -39% below the $0.75 Oct 1 placement price.

findings.finding: On 2026-11-11 Veritone moved its Q3 release and call from Nov 12 (after close) to Mon Nov 16 at 08:30 ET, explicitly 'to allow it additional time to provide material updates on the status of its convertible debt discussions'. That puts the outcome of the ~$45.6m 1.75% converts, which mature Sun 2026-11-15, inside the window. It also keeps a live Q&A call, and the company issued an ordinary product release (Box integration) on Nov 12. Neither fits a Chapter 11 filing, which a ~$50m market cap against $45.6m of debt partly discounts.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Nov 2025 note repurchase and term-loan payoff came with the Q3 2025 print: -10.6% (11-06 amc) and -5.95% (11-10 bmo). The Oct 2025 VDR hyperscaler contract wins plus an outlook update gave +53.7%. The Oct 1 2026 $15m registered direct for convert repayment drew about -37% that day (Benzinga, via search). So financing news has moved this stock by double digits in both directions.
findings.why_not_priced: The stock made a new all-time low after the notice (-7.8% on Nov 11 per Morningstar, $0.46 on Nov 13), so the market read the delay as bad or neutral. It is not priced as a resolved restructuring. If the market expected a clean extension, the stock would trade back toward the $0.75 price at which an institution bought 20m shares on Oct 1, knowing the proceeds were for 'repay and/or restructure a portion of its convertible debt'. That the company is holding the call is an inference about the outcome, not a disclosed term.
findings.independence: Separate document: the Nov 12 'Veritone Integrates with Box' release (https://investors.veritone.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/444/veritone-integrates-with-box) shows normal operations the day after the delay. The Oct 1 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001615165/000119312526409847/d42732dex991.htm) and the Q2 call, where the CFO cited active talks with holders (https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/veritone-inc-q2-2026-earnings-123000932.html), show discussions running for months. Both bear only on whether a deal exists, not on its terms.

findings.finding: The balance sheet cannot repay the notes. The Q2 10-Q shows cash of $12.4m at 2026-06-30, a $53.1m working-capital deficit, a going-concern flag and $45.58m of converts due 2026-11-15. H1 operating cash burn was about $22m. After the ~$1.8m July-August ATM and ~$14m net from the Oct 1 placement, cash going into maturity is roughly $15-20m (my estimate). Any resolution announced Nov 16 therefore needs large holder concessions: a debt-for-equity exchange at or below a $0.46 share price on ~122m shares, new secured paper, or an extension with a paydown. Each dilutes or subordinates the equity.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Oct 1 2026 dilutive raise was about -37% on the day. The Nov 2025 partial repurchase (about $39m cash plus 625k shares for $45.7m of principal) traded -6% to -11% around the print.
findings.why_not_priced: The deficit itself is public and largely in the price: market cap is about $55m against $45.6m of notes, and the stock is 39% below the Oct placement. The terms are not public. What would show if the market had priced a heavily dilutive exchange is a stock trading near the per-share recovery of a debt-for-equity swap. That value cannot be computed without the terms, which no one outside the negotiation has.
findings.independence: Oct 1 8-K exhibit 99.1 states proceeds go to 'repay and/or restructure a portion of its convertible debt' (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001615165/000119312526409847/d42732dex991.htm). The 10-Q post-quarter ATM note ($1.8m) is in the same 10-Q document.

findings.finding: The FY2026 revenue guide of $100-115m (cut on 2026-08-13 from $130-145m) needs H2 revenue of $55.5-70.5m, which is $27.8-35.3m a quarter. Q2 revenue was $24.3m and Q3 consensus is $25.6m. Management blamed VDR deal timing and DoD fund reallocation, so a second cut, or an H2 that depends on Q4 VDR deals, is likely on Nov 16.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (2026-08-13): revenue $24.3m against a $28.3m estimate plus a guide cut gave -22.8%. Q1 2026 (05-12) gave -11.7%. FY2025 results with a restatement delay (03-26) gave -29.5%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the stock has fallen about 75% since the guide cut. But consensus Q3 revenue of $25.6m sits inside a guide that still implies about $28-35m a quarter. If the market held the low end as the base case, the 52-week low would not be repeatedly broken into the print; if it had priced a further cut, sell-side estimates would sit below the guide's low end. Single-source consensus caps the size.
findings.independence: Q2 call summary on the VDR re-timing and DoD delays (https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/veritone-inc-q2-2026-earnings-123000932.html), a different document from the same company. Q2 bookings were $13.9m, -6.8% year on year.

findings.finding: The stock has been below $1 since the Oct 1 placement priced at $0.75. Thirty consecutive business days elapsed around Nov 12, so a Nasdaq minimum-bid deficiency letter (8-K item 3.01) could land in the window. EDGAR shows no filing after 2026-10-01 so far.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None for this name; a 180-day cure period usually makes these notices small movers.
findings.why_not_priced: It is widely anticipated on retail boards (StockTitan and Stocktwits posts expect it about 11/12), so it is mostly priced; it would only add to a negative headline cluster.
findings.independence: Stocktwits posts (https://stocktwits.com/symbol/VERI) expect the notice; these are speculation, not documents.

findings.finding: Short interest was 12.68m shares at 2026-10-30, with 7.78 days to cover. That is about 10% of ~122m shares outstanding, and about 29% if StockTitan's 43.7m float figure is right. Retail boards are framing Monday as a debt-resolution binary. Any non-bankruptcy outcome meets a short base that needs nearly 8 days of volume to cover.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The +53.7% on the Oct 2025 contract news and the +22.9% on Aug 2025 were both from a beaten-down base. Short interest fell 4m shares into the Oct 15 settlement (11.5m average volume that period) as the placement printed, so shorts do cover on financing news.
findings.why_not_priced: The short re-built (+0.53m) into 10-30 at an all-time-low price, so shorts are positioned for the bad branch. A priced benign outcome would show covering and the stock back above the $0.75 placement price.
findings.independence: The StockTitan float figure (https://www.stocktitan.net/news/VERI/veritone-updates-date-of-third-quarter-2026-earnings-release-and-ji9vtie38wee.html) is a different source for the float denominator; the short count itself is single-source (FINRA via Equibles).

outside_window.finding: Securities class action filed May 2026 (lead-plaintiff deadline July 20, 2026) following the FY2025 restatement and 4.02 non-reliance; litigation runs for years and does not resolve in this window.
Further cost cuts of $3.5-8.5m targeted by year-end 2026, aimed at non-GAAP breakeven in FY2027 on $125-130m of annualised revenue; this resolves over 2027, not on this print.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Veritone One divestiture for up to $104m as a cash source for the notes
rejected_candidates.detail: The sale closed in October 2024 and its proceeds went to the term loan (FY2024 10-K), so it is not a 2026 event. The only possible residual, the $18m earnout, is not shown as receivable in the Q2 2026 10-Q excerpt.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Q3 2025 revenue $29.1m beat as a year-on-year comparison base
rejected_candidates.detail: The comparison is already carried in the guidance finding's arithmetic; prior-year figures were revised in the restatement.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Retail board claim that 'an institution bought ~$15M without knowing the deal' as evidence of a pre-negotiated benign restructuring
rejected_candidates.detail: Merged into finding 1's why_not_priced (the Oct 1 placement at $0.75); the board post adds no document.

baseline_tension: There is no skew to agree or disagree with. The tape (all-time low, -15% over 20 days, -39% below the placement price) discounts a bad debt outcome. My findings split around that: the meeting-not-bankruptcy and crowded-short signals cut against the tape, and the cash gap and likely guide cut agree with it. So p_up sits near 50 and all the conviction goes into the size of the move, not its sign.
lessons_applied: Lesson 5 (documents beat inference): finding 1 rests on inference (holding a call implies no Chapter 11), not a disclosed term, so it was cut from +4.0 to +3.0.

Lesson 4 (financing is a question): asked what the Oct $15m buys. The answer is partial repayment of the converts under a going-concern flag, not funding for a ramp, so the cash-gap negative (-3.0) stands.
Lesson 7 (crowded short shrinks negatives): about 10-29% of float short with 7.8 days to cover, so the guidance negative went from -3.0 to -2.5 and the Nasdaq notice from -0.5 to -0.3.
Lesson 6 (bar): the Q3 revenue consensus has one source, so print_vs_bar is kept small (-4%). The guidance finding stays because it is arithmetic on the company's own guide.
Lesson 8 (thin coverage, understatement): abs_move kept at 30, well above the 17.2% historical median, because of the binary debt outcome. p_up was left at 52.
